dedupe_keys.name: colorado hotel2hospital guidebook for converting hotels into alternate care facilities during medical surge

description: This case study describes the development, proof-of-concept validation and operating framework of the Hotel2Hospital Conversion Guidebook, which shows hospital emergency managers how to turn a suitable hotel into an alternate care facility that delivers hospital-level care during a prolonged medical surge. It was written by Team Colorado, a group of emergency, hospitalist and virtual medicine physicians, emergency management professionals and other specialists working with the University of Colorado Hospital (UCH), and published in a peer-reviewed journal. The guidebook covers activation, operations and demobilisation, including information technology connectivity to the parent hospital, and was tested in a proof-of-concept conversion. Coverage is one US state, but the method is intended to transfer to other hospitals and to defence medical planning. The abstract is freely available; the full article is published under the publisher's terms, so access to the full text may require a subscription. Caveats: it is a single validation, and costs and patient outcomes of a real activation are not reported in the abstract. The study concluded that hotel conversion is a viable, scalable alternate care strategy for prolonged surges such as mass-casualty incidents, pandemics or wartime casualty repatriation. Simulation uses: a reference for surge capacity planning and emergency response scenarios that add temporary hospital beds. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy patient surge study (case_study-hurricane-sandy-nyc-hospital-evacuations) describes a real surge.
